recipes.name: Aloo paratha
instructions: Boil the potato until soft, then peel and mash it completely in a mixing bowl.
Add finely chopped onion, green chilli, and coriander leaves to the mashed potato and mix well.
In a separate bowl, add whole wheat flour and gradually mix with water to knead into a smooth, soft dough.
Divide the dough and the potato stuffing into two equal portions.
Roll out a portion of dough into a small circle, place the potato stuffing in the center, and fold the edges to seal it.
Flatten the stuffed dough ball and gently roll it out into a thick circular paratha.
Heat a tawa or griddle over medium heat and place the rolled paratha on it.
Cook both sides on the tawa until golden-brown spots appear, pressing gently with a spatula.

recipes.name: Mooli paratha
instructions: Grate the radish finely using a grater and place it in a large bowl.
Squeeze the grated radish firmly between your palms to extract and discard the excess water completely.
Mix the squeezed radish with finely chopped green chilli and coriander leaves in a bowl to make the filling.
Mix whole wheat flour with water in a separate bowl and knead into a pliable dough.
Divide the dough and the radish filling into two equal portions.
Take one dough ball, roll it slightly, place the radish filling in the center, and pleat the edges to cover the filling.
Dust with flour and roll carefully into a round paratha without tearing.
Place the paratha on a hot griddle and cook both sides until evenly browned and cooked through.

recipes.name: Gobi paratha
instructions: Grate the cauliflower florets finely and finely chop the onion, green chilli, and coriander leaves.
Combine the grated cauliflower, onion, green chilli, and coriander leaves in a mixing bowl for the stuffing.
Combine whole wheat flour with water and knead it into a soft dough, then let it rest for five minutes.
Divide the dough into two equal balls and roll each ball into a small thick disc.
Place half of the cauliflower mixture in the center of a disc, bring the edges together, and pinch to seal.
Gently roll the stuffed ball into a flat circular paratha using dry flour for dusting.
Place the paratha on a preheated tawa and cook on medium flame.
Flip and cook the other side until both surfaces have distinct golden spots and are thoroughly cooked.

recipes.name: Onion poha
instructions: Place the flattened rice in a colander, rinse it gently under running water, drain completely, and set aside to soften.
Finely chop the onion, green chilli, and coriander leaves, and dice the potato into very small cubes.
Heat a non-stick pan, add the diced potatoes, cover and cook on low heat until they are tender and lightly browned.
Add the chopped onions and curry leaves to the pan with the potatoes and sauté until the onions turn translucent.
Add the chopped green chillies and stir for a minute to release their flavor.
Add the rinsed and softened flattened rice to the pan and toss gently to combine all ingredients without mashing.
Cover the pan with a lid and let it steam on low heat for two to three minutes.
Turn off the heat, garnish with fresh coriander leaves, and mix gently before serving.

recipes.name: Matar poha
instructions: Rinse the flattened rice thoroughly in a sieve, drain all water, and let it rest to become soft.
Finely chop the onion and green chilli, and chop the coriander leaves for garnish.
In a pan, steam or dry-sauté the green peas and chopped onions until the onions are soft and peas are tender.
Add the chopped green chillies and curry leaves to the pan and sauté for another minute.
Gently add the softened flattened rice to the pan, blending it carefully with the vegetables.
Cover the pan and let the poha cook in its own steam on low heat for three minutes.
Uncover the pan and give it a final gentle stir to ensure uniform mixing.
Garnish with chopped coriander leaves and serve warm.

recipes.name: Vegetable upma
instructions: Add semolina to a dry pan and roast it over medium heat until it becomes fragrant and lightly golden, then transfer to a plate.
Finely chop the onion, carrot, and green chilli.
In the same pan, add the chopped onions, carrots, green peas, and curry leaves, and dry-sauté until they begin to soften.
Add the chopped green chilli and pour two and a half cups of water into the pan, bringing it to a rolling boil.
Once the water boils, lower the heat and slowly add the roasted semolina while stirring continuously to prevent lumps.
Keep stirring as the semolina absorbs the water and thickens into a uniform consistency.
Cover the pan with a lid and let the upma simmer on low heat for two to three minutes.
Turn off the heat and let it rest covered for a minute before fluffing and serving.

recipes.name: Palak paratha
instructions: Wash the spinach leaves thoroughly, blanch them in boiling water for two minutes, and drain completely.
Purée the blanched spinach leaves along with the green chilli in a blender until smooth.
Finely chop the onion.
In a large bowl, mix whole wheat flour, chopped onion, and the prepared spinach purée.
Knead the mixture into a soft, smooth dough, adding a little water if necessary.
Divide the dough into two equal portions and roll each portion into a smooth ball.
Roll out each ball into a circular flatbread of even thickness using dry flour for dusting.
Place the paratha on a hot tawa, cook both sides until dark green patches appear and it is thoroughly baked.

recipes.name: Methi paratha
instructions: Wash the fenugreek leaves thoroughly, drain completely, and chop them very finely.
Finely chop the onion and green chilli.
Combine the whole wheat flour, chopped fenugreek leaves, chopped onion, and green chilli in a large mixing bowl.
Mix the ingredients well and gradually add water to knead into a firm yet soft dough.
Divide the kneaded dough into two equal portions and shape them into round balls.
Roll out each dough ball into a round paratha using a rolling pin and a lightly floured surface.
Pre-heat a griddle and place the rolled paratha onto it, cooking on medium heat.
Flip the paratha and cook the other side, pressing gently with a clean cloth or spatula until fully cooked.

recipes.name: Dalia upma
instructions: Dry-roast the broken wheat in a pan over medium flame for four to five minutes until it turns aromatic.
Finely chop the onion, carrot, french beans, and green chilli.
In a pan or pressure cooker, dry-sauté the chopped onions, carrots, and french beans along with curry leaves until slightly tender.
Add the chopped green chilli and the roasted broken wheat to the pan, stirring to combine.
Pour three cups of water into the mixture and bring it to a boil.
Lower the heat, cover the pan tightly with a lid, and let it simmer for twelve to fifteen minutes until the dalia is cooked and water is absorbed.
Turn off the heat and keep the pan covered for an additional two minutes to let it finish steaming.
Uncover, fluff the dalia upma gently with a fork, and serve hot.

recipes.name: Vegetable mix paratha
instructions: Boil the potato and carrot until soft, then peel and mash them thoroughly in a bowl.
Finely grate the cauliflower florets and finely chop the onion, green chilli, and coriander leaves.
Combine the mashed potato, carrot, grated cauliflower, chopped onion, green chilli, and coriander leaves to make the vegetable filling.
Mix whole wheat flour with water and knead it into a smooth pliable dough.
Divide the dough into two equal parts and shape them into neat balls.
Roll a dough ball slightly, place half of the mixed vegetable filling inside, and pinch the edges together to seal well.
Flatten the stuffed ball and roll it out gently into a round paratha, ensuring the filling does not leak.
Cook the paratha on a hot griddle on both sides until even golden-brown spots form and the flatbread is completely cooked.
